card.title: AIR STRIPS
card.text: Add BREDA Ba.65 to hand and RM ROMA on top of your deck.
card.flavorText: Throughout WWII, the Italian Regia Aeronautica relied heavily on improvised forward air strips to support fast-moving campaigns and overcome infrastructure limitations. In North Africa, Italian forces constructed temporary runways across Libya and into Egypt, often using materials like packed sand or metal matting to support operations in harsh desert conditions. These air strips allowed bombers and fighters to stay close to the front but were vulnerable to dust, heat and enemy attacks. In the Balkans, Italy used both captured and newly built airfields in Albania, Greece, and Yugoslavia to maintain air superiority and support occupation forces. Many of these sites were hastily prepared, relying on local labor and limited resources. Across Mediterranean islands like Pantelleria, Sardinia and Sicily, airfields served both as defensive positions and springboards for offensive sorties. These were frequently targeted by Allied raids, especially in 1943 during the lead-up to Operation Husky. On the Eastern Front, Italian air units operated from crude, often muddy fields in southern Russia, struggling with poor weather and logistics. Despite challenges, these air strips enabled continued support for Axis ground operations in every major theater where Italian forces fought.
